sources.title: Central African Republic Country Climate and Development Report: Resilient and Inclusive Growth—Sustainable Solutions for CAR's Future
sources.temporal_coverage: 2020 baseline; urban flood projections to 2050 and 2100 across SSP-RCP pathways; broader CCDR uses historical indicators.
sources.methodology: CCDR combines diagnostics, spatial exposure analysis and climate/economic scenarios.
sources.limitations: Scenario-dependent model; French OCR imperfect; no causal violence estimate.

sources.title: Central African Republic Humanitarian Situation Report No. 2 (End-of-Year), reporting period 1 January to 31 December 2025
sources.temporal_coverage: Operational results and humanitarian events during 2025; reporting period 1 January-31 December 2025.
sources.methodology: UNICEF annual operational monitoring and partner-reported humanitarian results.
sources.limitations: Operational reporting, not causal evaluation; flood locations and climate-attributable shares are not disaggregated.

claims.paraphrase: Drought exposure exceeds the national average in Equateur, Yade and Oubangui; about one-third of Bangui residents face flood exposure, with poor households especially vulnerable.

claims.locator: Printed p. 58, urban exposure analysis and footnote 61
claims.paraphrase: CCDR models flooding in Bangui, Bambari, Birao and Berberati; in Bangui, 60% of flood-exposed buildings are informal, alongside exposed schools, roads and hospitals.
claims.scenario: Flood estimates compare 2020, 2050 and 2100 under four SSP-RCP pathways.
claims.limitations: Exposed assets, not all city assets.

claims.paraphrase: CCDR says climate extremes reduce yields and intensify land/water competition, raising conflict and displacement risks.
claims.limitations: National pathway, not causal estimate; conflict has other drivers.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Climate shocks and resource competition raise conflict/displacement risks.

claims.paraphrase: CCDR options include climate-resilient pastoral systems, corridor oversight, water points and local committees able to arbitrate farmer-herder disputes.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Corridor works can help local committees arbitrate farmer-herder disputes.

claims.locator: PDF p. 2, situation overview and humanitarian needs
claims.paraphrase: June-November 2025 flooding damaged homes, schools, health facilities and livelihoods and drove displacement in flood-prone areas; the report does not name affected flood locations.
claims.limitations: Annual situation report does not provide flood counts or distinguish climate change from seasonal flood hazard.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The report states seasonal flooding damaged livelihoods and drove displacement.

claims.locator: PDF p. 2, security and humanitarian access update
claims.paraphrase: Armed attacks increased in the South-East and North-East, violence continued in the North-West, and 61 agency bases closed; insecurity further limited humanitarian access.
claims.limitations: The report does not attribute these access constraints specifically to climate-response operations.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: UNICEF says insecurity further limited humanitarian access.

claims.locator: PDF pp. 1 and 3, results highlights and WASH response
claims.paraphrase: UNICEF reports water access for 23,539 people and 95 water-point committees established or revitalized; So Fini's late-2025 multisector response addressed six shocks.
claims.limitations: Reported operational outputs are not an evaluation of durable resilience or equitable coverage.

access_audit.notes: Full 92-page French CCDR opened; reviewed urban exposure, regional household exposure, climate-fragility pathway and pastoral options. OCR has gaps/garbling in places.
access_audit.reuse_terms: World Bank publication permits noncommercial reproduction with full attribution; additional permissions may apply.

access_audit.notes: Full 13-page 2025 end-year situation report inspected for floods, displacement, insecurity/access constraints and reported WASH response outputs.
IOM Crisis Response Plan 2026 page returned HTTP 403; search excerpts were not used to support claims.

search_audit.query: Central African Republic prefecture city flood drought climate exposure vulnerability
search_audit.outcome: Opened the World Bank CCDR and UNICEF's full 2025 SitRep; CCDR identifies named urban and regional exposure, while the SitRep lacks flood-location disaggregation.

search_audit.query: Central African Republic climate shocks land water competition conflict displacement source report
search_audit.outcome: CCDR explicitly describes lower yields and competition for land/water as raising conflict and displacement risks; it does not estimate causal shares or establish climate as the sole driver.

search_audit.query: Central African Republic insecurity humanitarian access climate response capacity flood displacement 2025
search_audit.outcome: UNICEF reports insecurity further constrained humanitarian access and also separately records flood-related displacement; it does not establish an effect of conflict on climate-adaptation delivery specifically.

search_audit.query: Central African Republic pastoral resilience water points local farmer herder arbitration climate capacity
search_audit.outcome: CCDR recommends corridor infrastructure and local dispute-arbitration capacity; UNICEF reports water-point committees, access outputs and So Fini shock response, not durable impact evaluation.

gaps: UNICEF's 2025 flood/displacement summary does not identify affected prefectures or separate seasonal flooding from climate-change attribution.
CCDR's conflict pathway is a modeled/analytical risk framing; it does not establish climate-caused violence or quantify causal contribution.
The IOM Crisis Response Plan 2026 page returned HTTP 403; no findings from its search excerpt were used.
Operational WASH and response outputs are not independently evaluated household resilience outcomes.
